name: get_context
summary: Read issue, project, decision or input request context by key or id
description: Read one issue, project, decision, input request, or artifact by key or id. Issue context comes from the issue context endpoint; project context is markdown. Pass comments:true to include the issue thread. Use the input-request id to inspect a human's answer. Example: {"id":"BUG-142"}.

id.description: Key or id: BUG-142, ADR-21, in_…, pj_…, ir_…, ar_….

type.description: Only when the kind cannot be inferred from the id.

comments.description: Issues only: include the comment thread (last 20).

name: find_work
summary: Find issues, input requests or decisions with filters (assignee `me`, status, project…)
description: Find issues to work on or existing human input requests and decisions. scope: all (default: issues), issues, input_requests (default state open), decisions. Filters: q, assignee ('me' or user id), status, priority, kind, projectId, teamId, issueId, open (default true for issues), and limit. Global request/decision listings include legacy records without an issue link. Use get_context for detail.

issueId.description: Optional issue filter for human input and decisions.

assignee.description: 'me' or a user id (assignee for issues and input requests).

status.description: Status of the selected scope: issue, input request, or decision status.

name: search
summary: Full-text search across every object type; run it before creating anything
description: Full-text search across supported object types: issues, projects, decisions, artifacts, repositories, teams and customers. Run it before creating anything so you reuse what exists. `types` narrows the results. Returns type, id, key, title and subtitle.

name: get_insights
summary: Where the problems are: stale or overdue issues, bottlenecks, stuck PRs, flow metrics, agent failures
description: Where are the problems? Health signals for blocked or stale issues, bottlenecks, PRs stuck in review, failing CI, undecided decisions, customer demand waiting, flow metrics and agent failures. Use it to decide what needs attention before picking work. Narrow with projectId or teamId; days is 7, 30 or 90. The full list behind one signal: run_tool {name:'get_insight_signal', arguments:{id:'<signal>'}}.

name: get_workspace
summary: Workspace settings: label ids, estimate scale
description: The workspace and its settings: label catalog (ids to pass as `labels`), estimateScale (none, fibonacci, linear, exponential, tshirt), customer tiers. Read it once before filing issues so you assign real label ids and a valid estimate. Takes no arguments.

name: list_repositories
summary: Registered git repositories (maps a checkout to its project)
description: Registered git repositories (id, provider, fullName, url). To find the project of a git checkout, match its remote's owner/name to `fullName` (case-insensitive, after following any rename), then use the id with list_projects. No match means the checkout is not registered: say so, do not guess.

name: list_projects
summary: Projects; filter by repository to find the project of a checkout
description: Projects contain related issues and planning context. Filter by repositoryId to find the project of this checkout, or by q, status, teamId, leadId. One match is 'this project'; several: ask which. Then find_work {projectId} lists its issues and get_context {id:'pj_…'} reads it whole.

name: create_issue
description: File one issue after checking for duplicates. Issues are the sole unit of work; set a concise goal when it helps clarify the desired result. source defaults to agent. Labels are ids from get_workspace settings.labels, never names.

title.description: The symptom or request in plain words, under ~80 chars.

body.description: Markdown: steps, expected vs actual, where you saw it.

estimate.description: Only when the size is clear and the workspace uses estimates.

force.description: Create even if an open issue has the same title.

name: update_issue
summary: Change an issue's status, priority, assignee, labels, duplicate marker…
description: Update one issue: status, priority, assignee, labels, estimate, title/body, project, kind (re-keys it), duplicateOfId (marks a duplicate of another issue). null clears an optional field. Set in_progress when you start (the server assigns you if you are a user and nobody is), in_review while the PR is open, done ONLY once the fix is merged. Never close what you did not verify. Several issues at once: triage_issues. Example: {"idOrKey":"BUG-142","status":"in_review"}.

name: start_work
summary: Pick up an issue: context, safety checks, marks the start
description: Start work on an issue: load issue context, inspect linked questions and decisions, and set the issue in_progress. Completed and canceled issues are not changed. Pass a short plan to leave it as a comment.

plan.description: One comment: what you will do.

name: report_progress
summary: Record artifacts, issue status, project update and a comment
description: Record issue or project progress: artifact, issueStatus, projectUpdate, and/or comment. Do not set an issue done until its fix is verified and merged.

issue.description: Issue key or id (for issueStatus, artifacts and comments).

project.description: Project id (for projectUpdate, artifacts and comments).

externalId.description: PR number, sha, build id: used to find the existing artifact.

description.description: Only used when the artifact is created.

issueStatus.description: New status of `issue`. in_review while its PR is open; done only once merged.

comment.description: One factual comment on the issue or project.

name: ask_human
summary: Ask a person one question (an input request), once
description: One Human input feature with two modes. mode=question creates an input request linked to an issue; a human answers it later, preserving the request lifecycle. mode=decision proposes a lasting decision linked to the issue; a human accepts, rejects or supersedes it. Question mode is the default.

mode.description: Question request (default) or a lasting decision proposal.

statement.description: Proposed rule or choice (required in decision mode).

rationale.description: Why this decision is needed, including alternatives.

name: record_decision
summary: Propose a lasting decision (a person accepts it)
description: Propose a lasting decision attached to an issue. A person must accept, reject or supersede it; the agent never accepts its own proposal. Pass originIssue or issue to associate it.

decision.description: Existing decision key/id to edit instead of creating.

name: attach_artifact
summary: Attach or update a PR, build, document or link on an issue or project
description: Attach proof of work or a reference to an issue or project: pull request, build, test report, deployment, design, document or link. Idempotent when the same external id or URL is repeated.

externalId.description: PR number, sha, build id: used to find the existing artifact.

description.description: What it is / why attached (only used on create).

name: add_comment
summary: Comment on any object by key or id
description: Comment on an issue or decision by key or id. Use for a factual note after a meaningful step; skip trivial steps because the activity log records changes.

on.description: Key or id of what you comment on.

type.description: Only when the kind cannot be inferred.

name: triage_issues
summary: Triage up to 25 issues in one call (priority, duplicates, grouping)
description: Triage up to 25 issues in one call: priority, duplicate marker, assignment, project, status, labels, and comment. Items fail independently.

duplicateOf.description: Key or id of the original issue.

name: list_capabilities
summary: Discover the full catalog: search it, get a tool's schema and how to call it
description: Discover the long tail beyond this tool list: every Trama operation your key may use (137 catalog operations: teams, projects, milestones, customers, views, webhooks, members…). No arguments: groups with counts. q or group: matching tools with a one-line summary. tool:'<name>': full detail with the exact input schema and how to call it. Then run it with run_tool. Use it when none of the task tools above fits, instead of guessing names. Example: {"q":"milestone"} then {"tool":"create_milestone"}.

q.description: Words that must all appear in a tool's name, description or route.

group.description: Resource group, e.g. issues, projects, milestones, teams, customers.

tool.description: Exact tool name: returns its schema and call example.

all.description: Also list tools your key cannot use (marked unavailable).

name: run_tool
summary: Run any catalog operation by name, with the usual validation and permissions
description: Run any operation found with list_capabilities by its name, with that tool's own arguments. Arguments are validated against the tool's schema and the API checks your key's permissions on every call, exactly as if the tool were listed. Example: {"name":"create_milestone","arguments":{"projectId":"pj_…","name":"Beta"}}. For a route no tool covers use api_request.
